Comprises natural heroin adulterated with caffeine, paracetamol, and MDMA; sold at 1,000 to 6,000–8,000 DZD depending on quantity and quality, with police seizures equating 4.9 kg of heroin to 490,000 doses (10 mg per dose).
source: Le Jour d'Algérie; Ultra Algeria; La Patrie News; L'Expression; DGSN University Lectures

spelling variants: el chouchena, chouchna, chouchana, الشوشنة, شوشنة
notes: De-affricated phonetic variant of تشوشنة (dropping the initial t-) widely used in Algiers street vernacular and investigative reporting for adulterated brown/black heroin. Polysemy warning: refers to small pouches or tassels in traditional dialectal usage.
source: Ultra Algeria ('الشوشنة في الجزائر: مخدرات تقتل بسرعة')

spelling variants: مسحوق بني, المخدرات السوداء, الأسمر, brown, black
notes: Descriptive physical-state terms used in Algerian toxicological and investigative profiles for the two street presentations of heroin and tchouchna: brown powder (مسحوق بني / brown sugar) and solid black chunks (قطع صلبة سوداء اللون / black tar).
source: Ultra Algeria; Algerian University Narcotics Awareness Presentations

spelling variants: ho9na, 7oqna, حقنة, حقن, بحقنها, على الوريد, تحت الجلد, injection
notes: Terms denoting syringe administration of heroin or tchouchna either intravenously (على الوريد) or subcutaneously (تحت الجلد), a high-lethality consumption route documented in fatal Algiers overdose cases. Polysemy warning: refers to any medical injection in clinical dialogue.
source: Ultra Algeria; Ennahar Online & Algérie 360 (Bab El Oued overdose court reports)

spelling variants: سيبتيكس, سوبوتاكس, سوبوتكس, septik, soubra, subu, buprénorphine
notes: Buprenorphine, a synthetic opioid medication listed on Algeria's high-risk controlled substances decree; diverted on the black market (as سوبوتاكس, سيبتيكس, or soubra) and grouped alongside painkillers and opioids in addiction reports.
source: Algerian Customs Interministerial Decree (11 Aug 2021); Al Jazeera; Echorouk Online; Sky News Arabia

spelling variants: افيون, الأوبيوم, المورفين, ميثادون, opium, morphine, methadone
notes: Opiate class terms; clinical toxicology at CHU Bab-El-Oued ranks morphine alongside pregabalin and cannabis as the top three molecules detected in acute intoxications, while methadone is deployed in Algerian addiction centers for heroin withdrawal.
source: CHU Bab-El-Oued Toxicology Study (AJOL); Ultra Algeria

spelling variants: heroine, heroin, الهيروين, الهيرويين, الهرويين
notes: Standard French and Arabic clinical/legal designation; exhibits high orthographic instability in Arabic script across Algerian publications (single vs. double ya, presence or absence of first ya: هيروين / هيرويين / هرويين).
source: Personal knowledge (orthographic variants verified across Ennahar, Al Jazeera & ASJP)

spelling variants: كودايين, الكوديين, البثيدين, codeine, codéine, péthidine
notes: Pharmaceutical opiates and synthetic opioid analgesics classified alongside morphine and heroin under sedative opioid narcotics in Algerian academic toxicology.
source: Université de Guelma / Université d'Annaba Academic Toxicology Literature

spelling variants: شوشنة بيضاء, el chouchena el beida, chouchna bayda
notes: Literally 'white chouchena'; a higher-purity or differently cut variant of Tchouchna (adulterated heroin) consumed by addicts progressing between cocaine (الخيط) and black Tchouchna.
source: Algerian Investigative Press (El Hiwar / El-Massa)

spelling variants: سبيتاك, el sbeitak, sbitak, sbeitak
notes: Vernacular Algerian phonetic spelling of Subutex (buprenorphine), documented as a fallback opioid substitute used when addicts exhaust their money on cocaine (الخيط) and الشوشنة.
source: Algerian Investigative Press (El Hiwar / El-Massa)

spelling variants: حزمة, 7azma, hazma, الباراسيتامول
notes: Packaging and adulteration terminology: retail heroin is seized in small wraps/bundles (حزم) in Algiers neighborhoods like Bab El Oued, and dealers frequently cut it with crushed الباراسيتامول (paracetamol) to mimic high-grade heroin.
source: Algiers Judicial & Police Seizure Reports (Ennahar / El-Massa)
